title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 19)
summary: Part 19 of his commentary on Marcus Aurelius's Meditations, linking the passage on being a member of humanity to his individualism video. He covers owning your power, not letting others change your principles, upsetting yourself, accepting change, loving those who insult you, a disagreement with Marcus about wrathful looks, and the value of daily solitude.
claims: Marcus's idea of being a member, not merely a part, of humanity mirrors his individualism thesis: bettering yourself as a member benefits the collective, which benefits you back
Be careful how you describe your life to yourself, because the words dictate how you live it
You cannot stop pain signals but you can choose to ignore them; many people refuse to admit their own power because admitting it makes every mishap their responsibility
Whiny groups attract and convert others because blame culture is comfortable, and joining one is the worst thing you can do
Never change your principles in reaction to others, even when it would be convenient; evolve only for your own sake
Systems that try to stop crime at the source, by restricting weapons or engineering children, are diseased; respond to actions instead of preventing them
When you are upset you upset yourself; an insult only hurts if you are not fully confident that it is false
Humans are agents of change and therefore its main victims; treat change as neutral, and see systems that try to control change as either malicious or naive
YouTube fitness is the most negative category on the platform; people insult you because they feel bad about themselves, and they deserve pity
Help others when you can, but preserve yourself at all costs; kind people who overextend lose touch with the self and can turn bad
He disagrees with Marcus on wrathful looks: an angry look is a social warning that prevents violence; the dog that does not bark is the one that bites
When insulted, intellectualize why the person said it instead of reacting; do not weaponize empathy, except to jolt awake someone who is a lost case
Do not feel superior when an attack fails to land; the attacker is only erring in that moment and you could do the same
Take moments every day without phone, book or TV to simply think; if you cannot sit still like that, it signals anxiety that needs fixing
